title: Recovery Systems
hook: I kept pushing harder and getting less done. Turns out I wasn't lazy, I was cooked.
statement: Growth needs recovery built in. Rest isn't a reward you earn later, it's part of the work.
explainer: Stress stacks up quietly. If recovery doesn't keep pace, you start making sloppy calls, snapping at people, and dreading the work. That's burnout showing up early.
sop: Rate your Stress and your Recovery from 1 to 10 right now.
Put recovery time on your calendar like a client call.
Pick one recovery habit, like sleep or a day off, and guard it for 2 weeks.
Watch for early signs each week: irritability, mistakes, dread.
If Stress ÷ Recovery stays above 1 for a few days, change something.
equation_example: Stress 8, Recovery 3. 8 ÷ 3 = 2.67. Anything above 1 means stress is outrunning recovery and burnout is coming. Flip it, Stress 4 and Recovery 8, and you get 0.5. That's a load you can carry.
question: Write down one recovery habit you keep treating as optional, and when you'll do it this week.
closing_statement: Recovery isn't the reward for growth. It's part of the fuel.
caption:
Principle Nº 139: Recovery Systems

I kept pushing harder and getting less done. Turns out I wasn't lazy, I was cooked.

Growth needs recovery built in. Rest isn't a reward you earn later, it's part of the work.

Your turn: Write down one recovery habit you keep treating as optional, and when you'll do it this week.
